post.description:
Resolve the options an upstream method's output slot offers.

The Inspector's options picker calls this for a parameter declared with
``options_from: <input>``, once per upstream wired to that input. Each
param set is filled with the version's declared defaults and the slot's
``options`` block is expanded over them with
``wfc.contracts.resolve_options``. A Run Reference upstream resolves
through its run: the run's method and version, and one param set, the
params it ran with. *method_full* is then not read (the canvas sends a
placeholder).

Args:
    method_full: ``module.method`` (e.g. ``features.regionprops``).
    request: The slot, and either the version and param sets or a run id.

Returns:
    ``{fixed, built: [{params, names}], patterns, all}`` in declaration
    order, each name once; ``patterns`` are returned literally (matching
    one needs the data, which is not read here). A Run Reference's
    answer also names the run's ``module`` and ``method``.

Raises:
    HTTPException: 400 for a method name with no dot or a run id that is
        not an integer; 404 for an unknown run, or, without a run id, an
        unknown module, method or version.

get.description:
List directory contents under the project root.

``path`` is relative to the project root. Defaults to the root itself.
Rejects any path that resolves outside the project root. Safe for a
localhost single-user dev tool: the server is already scoped to the
project the user chose to launch it against.

Return modules as a nested dict keyed by module/method name for the builder UI.

Shape: {moduleName: {description, color, methods: {methodName: {inputs,
outputs, params_schema, executor, env, description, versions}}, drafts:
{methodName: {kind, folder, ...contract, env, valid, reasons}}}}. The
method's own contract fields and env are its newest version's;
``versions`` lists every version (label, identity, registered_at, env,
newest) with its contract. ``color`` is the module's stored colour and
``drafts`` the module's drafts (the palette's Drafts group). The
builder's module palette reads this shape.

schema.title: Response Get Modules Api Modules Get

get.description:
Return ``<project_root>/demo-pipeline.json`` (written by ``wfc demo``).

Consumed by the ``?pipeline=demo`` URL param in the canvas, which hands
the document to ``loadPipeline()`` so each node's real slots resolve
against the registry. 404 when no demo is scaffolded — inert in a
normal project.

Return the run's literal frozen ``pipeline.json``.

Reads ``<project_root>/.wfc/runs/pipelines/<pipeline_id>/pipeline.json`` —
written at submission time for canvas runs, frozen at run start by
``run_pipeline`` for CLI runs, and the same file
``WfcProvider._load_bundled_samples`` consumes for fan-in sample
resolution. Returns the parsed JSON document as-is so the canvas can
hand it to ``loadPipeline()`` without transformation.

404 when the file does not exist (the pipeline was authored but
never reached the snake-gen / run-generation stage).

Serve a pipeline run's frozen ``pipeline.json`` as a file download.

The file is the run's frozen copy byte for byte: enrichment wrote every
method node's resolved version into it, so running the downloaded
document again runs the same versions.

Status codes:
  - 200 with the file as an ``attachment`` named
    ``<pipeline_id>.pipeline.json``
  - 400 for an id that names no single pipeline directory
  - 404 when the pipeline has no frozen document
List every draft, each with its Registration check and latest draft run.

post.description:
Add a method folder as a draft of a module.

The dry run states the kind (a DRAFT version of the module's method of
the folder's name, or a DRAFT method) and the dialog's sentence, writing
nothing. A folder whose method already has a draft from another folder
is a 400 naming that folder.
Check each draft's folder against its pointer's stat snapshot; nothing is written.

delete.description:
Remove draft: delete its draft folder (pointer and draft run); the method folder is untouched.

As method registration's route: the dry run returns Execution's delete
plan (what goes, the text ``wfc delete-draft`` prints) and its token,
deleting nothing. The real request sends the token back as ``planned``
and deletes only when a fresh plan has the same token; a different one
is a 409 having deleted nothing, and a request with no token is a 400.

get.description: The draft's Registration check: every line ✓ or ✗; nothing is written.
A draft's files and contract for its expanded row.

The dry run and the token as :func:`remove_registry_draft` takes them,
over the Delete outputs plan.

Download the draft run's outputs as a zip.

post.description:
Update: Registration's writing re-read of the draft, with no run.

The contract read now is stored on the pointer; the entry carries the
re-read's own Registration check. Nothing is registered.

get.description:
List distinct env specs referenced by registered methods.

One row per ``Method.env`` value. Lists the method names sharing that
env, takes its run count and most-recent run start from Execution's run
tallies (:func:`wfc.execution.run_tallies`), and resolves the registered env's ``backend``
plus a ``has_packages`` flag: whether the captures folder of the env's
current image holds a package list (a byo image's holds none). It does
not verify the list: ``GET .../packages`` does, and refuses one whose
bytes no longer match the record.

Each row's ``registry`` says where the env's images are, read from the
captures folders and the local daemon, never the registry: ``state``
(``pushed``, ``not_pushed``, ``none`` for no registry, ``cannot_push``
for an image on this machine whose env name no registry accepts,
``missing``, or ``unknown`` when Docker does not answer), ``base``,
``older_not_pushed`` (older images method versions record that are not
pushed), ``older_missing`` (versions whose older image is gone),
``recreate`` (the command that recreates the image), ``own_registry``
(for a byo image pulled from its own registry, that ref; else ``null``)
and ``reason`` (for ``cannot_push``, why the name cannot be pushed and
the fixes; else ``null``). It is ``null`` for an env with no record.

Installed-package list for a registered env.

Resolves *spec* to its :class:`wfc.environments.EnvRecord`, asks
Environments for the package list of the env's current image
(:func:`wfc.environments.verified_package_list`, read from the committed
captures folder and checked against the record's ``source_fingerprint``),
and parses it into a sorted, de-duplicated, source-tagged package list
via :func:`wfc.environments.parse_packages`.

Honest empty state: a byo env, an env that never staged source content,
or an unmatched spec returns ``captured: false`` with ``packages: []`` —
never a fabricated list. A captures folder changed outside wfc is a
409: a package list that is missing or whose bytes no longer match the
record, or an ``image.json`` that is missing or unreadable. Its detail
names the file and the remedy register-env's refusal names for the
same folder (:func:`wfc.environments.capture_remedy`): register the env
again under a new name.

Response::

    {"spec": "demo",
     "backend": "pixi" | "conda" | "uv" | "byo" | null,
     "captured": true,
     "packages": [{"name": ..., "version": ..., "source": "pixi"}, ...]}

List registered methods for the Registry tab.

Shape: `{methods: [{name, module, env, runCount, source, versions}]}`.

`source` is the project-relative `method.yaml` of the method's
registered copy, as the code resolver finds it, or null when the
resolver refuses the record. `versions` lists every version in label
order (:func:`_version_out`); the method's `env` is its newest
version's. A version is named by its identity in the detail and export
routes; the label is for display. The methods are Registration's
listing (:func:`~wfc.registration.list_methods`); the run counts are
Execution's run tallies (:func:`~wfc.execution.run_tallies`), merged on
the listed row ids.

post.description:
Wrap ``wfc.registration.register_method`` with optional dry-run preflight.

The dry run also plans the registration (``plan_method_registration``,
nothing written) and returns the plan's message, the same text ``wfc
register-method`` prints: registers v1, adds a version naming what
changed, or matches the newest version. Beside it the plan carries its
``label`` (the version it adds, or the newest it matches), the
``newestLabel`` before registering, its ``changes`` and ``holds`` as
Registration states them (the data the message is rendered from), and
its ``token``: the identity of what it would write (code fingerprint,
env fingerprint, newest label). A refusal the plan makes (a folder that
does not clearly hold one method among them) is a failed pre-check
whose detail says what wfc expects.
The Register click is the confirmation of that plan: the real request
sends the token back as ``plan_token`` and registration applies only
when a fresh plan has the same token, the rule ``wfc register-method``
applies between its question and its write. A different token (the
source, the env or the version list changed since the dry run) is a 409
having changed nothing; a request with no token is a 400.

get.description:
Read-only view of one version of a method: its files, contract and env.

Lists every file at the top of the version's extracted copy,
``.wfc/runs/code/<tree hash>/`` (no recursion), with its content and a
language hint for syntax highlighting: the method's main script first,
then the rest by name. Returns the version's DB-parsed contract
(input_slots, output_slots, params_schema, executor) alongside so the
frontend can render it as structured tables without re-parsing YAML,
and the version itself (:func:`_version_out`, with its run count).

Args:
    module_name: The method's module.
    method_name: The method's name.
    version: The version's content identity (what a pin holds); absent
        is the newest version. A version no entry carries is a 404.

Download one version of a method's script and contract as a zip.

The zip, ``<method>_v<label>.zip``, holds every file of the version's
registered copy as Registration resolves it (``resolve_method_code``),
subfolders included, under their copy-relative paths. The copy's
verified stamp sits beside the copy, not in it, so it is never in the
zip. Unzipped and edited, the folder registers as a new version.

Args:
    module_name: The method's module.
    method_name: The method's name.
    version: The version's content identity; absent is the newest
        version. A version no entry carries is a 404 naming it.

List registered modules for the Registry tab.

Shape: `{modules: [{name, description, contracts[], methods, source,
color}]}`. `color` is the module's stored colour (`#rrggbb`), the one
every view shows. The modules are Registration's listing

Return a synthesized literal-only lineage pipeline for ``run_id``.

Walks ``parentRunIds`` from the clicked run back to roots — through
pipeline boundaries — and synthesizes a flat literal-only pipeline
JSON suitable for the canvas's ``loadPipeline()``. See
``wfc.lineage.synthesis`` for the algorithm.

Status codes:
  - 200 with synthesized JSON on success
  - 404 if the run id is unknown
  - 422 if synthesis fails (cycle defense, malformed ancestor chain),
    or if the lineage holds a run whose record carries no version
    identity, so its node cannot be pinned to the version it ran; the
    ``detail`` names each such run and the canvas shows it as written

Read-only.  Counts come straight from the DB (progress truth is the DB);

Zip download of wfc run artifacts, optionally filtered by file type.

An invalid project config is a 409 with ``read_config``'s message.

Plan, or download, the run bundle of the requested runs.

The dry run plans the export (:func:`wfc.run_bundle.plan_export`: the
selection, Storage's archive pass over unarchived outputs, every
refusal, the local-only images) and returns ``{"plan": ...}``, the
plan's ``to_dict`` with its ``token``. It writes no bundle and answers
200 even when the plan is refused (``ok`` false).

The download is the confirmation of that plan: it sends the token back
as ``plan_token``, plans again, and writes the bundle only when the
fresh plan has the same token, the rule ``wfc export-run`` applies
between its question and its write. A request with no token is a 400; a
refused plan is a 409 listing every reason; a different token (the runs,
the options or what they hold changed since the dry run) is a 409. The
zip is written to a temporary file, streamed, and removed afterwards.

Reload the history provider for the project this canvas serves.

A canvas serves the one project it was launched in. Naming that project,
in any spelling that resolves to it, reloads the provider. Naming any
other project is refused with 409 and changes nothing: the canvas keeps
serving its project, and the message says to start a canvas in the other.

get.description:
Serve one artifact's bytes, typed and named by its displayed name.

The media type comes from ``artifact_path``, never the resolved cache
path (a top-level file output's cache entry has no extension). The file
is shown inline and saved under its displayed name; an SVG is sandboxed
so any script in it cannot run.

schema.title: Response List Wfc Artifacts Api Wfc Run  Run Id  Artifacts Get

get.description: Return runs cancelled because ``run_id`` (or its subtree) failed.

Say what the image route's preview of a raster image shows, read from its header.

The file's and the preview's dimensions, whether the bit depth is
reduced, its page count, the memory converting it takes, the smallest
``[previews] memory_mb`` that admits it, and why the image route would
refuse it. Never decodes the file. An SVG, any other kind and a file
Pillow cannot read are a 415.

Serve an image artifact as a PNG of at most 260, 2048 or 4096 px on its longer side.

Every raster image is converted, browser formats included, so the browser
never gets more than 4096 px; an image that fits ``size`` keeps its own
size. An SVG is served as it is, sandboxed. ``[previews] memory_mb`` is a
ceiling on the memory image previews use at once: two conversions run at
once and each may use up to half. An image whose conversion needs more,
reckoned from its header (decoded size plus the resize, 8-bit and encode
working images), is a 422 with its dimensions and the ``memory_mb`` that
would admit it, never decoded. ``image-info`` tells what the preview shows.

A converted PNG is kept in the preview cache (``[previews] cache_mb``,
least recently used dropped first), keyed by the output's content: a
second request for the same image and size is answered from it, without
converting or queueing. Otherwise conversions queue for the two
conversion threads, first come first served. The route is ``async`` so a
queued request holds none of the server's shared worker threads; the
config read and the path's resolution run on one, the decode on the
conversion pool.

200.description: The preview PNG; an SVG as it is, sandboxed.

415.description: Not a raster image or SVG, or a file Pillow cannot read.

422.description: Converting the image would need more than half of [previews] memory_mb; the body names the memory_mb that admits it (an invalid size is FastAPI's validation error).

get.description:
Preview the start of a table, JSON or text artifact, saying what was cut.

A table shows at most 100 rows read from at most 2 MB, its delimiter and
header row guessed unless ``delimiter`` or ``header`` is given; text shows
at most 1 MB; JSON is parsed up to 5 MB, and a larger or invalid file
comes back as text with its reason. Any other kind is a 415. An invalid
project config is a 409 with ``read_config``'s message.

Stream a run's stdout/stderr as SSE events, ending with a `terminal` event.

- Terminal runs (status in {completed, success, failed, cancelled})
  reached with no resume id: read the on-disk log files, emit each line
  as a `stdout`/`stderr` event, then emit the `terminal` event and
  close. ``?full=1`` returns the whole file; default tails the last
  ``tail`` lines (default 500).
- Running runs: emit a tail snapshot, then poll the log files every
  ~200 ms, emit new lines as they appear, stop when the DB status
  transitions off ``running`` and emit a final `terminal` event. Each
  live line's event carries an SSE ``id`` naming the stdout and stderr
  byte offsets read through it (the snapshot's end is marked by an
  id-only frame). A reconnect sending that id as ``Last-Event-ID`` (the
  browser's auto-reconnect does) opens with an id-only frame naming
  the same offsets, then resumes from them with no snapshot, so no line
  repeats and none is missed across a server restart. A run that ended
  while the connection was down gets only the bytes after the offsets,
  then its `terminal` event. An absent or malformed id gets the
  snapshot, as a first connection does.
Return detailed info for all registered samples.

post.description:
Cancel a running pipeline, in this server's job table or reached by its record.

Goes through Execution's one cancel operation: it sets the record's
cancel flag, kills the engine's process tree when its identity matches,
and flips the ``running`` rows to ``cancelled`` for the user; when the
pipeline's owner is gone it also gives every unstarted target a ``user``
row, releases what the pipeline held and removes the record. For a job
in this server's table the in-memory flag is set first, so its run
thread's failure branch leaves the rows to the cancel and its own end
steps walk with ``user``; a job whose process is not recorded (refused
before its record was written) has that process's tree killed here.

Idempotent: a pipeline whose engine has already exited answers 200 with
``noop: true``. An id with neither a job nor a record nor a running row,
or one that is not a pipeline id, answers 404.

Submit a pipeline for execution via Snakemake.

Enriches the PipelineJSON with script paths and slot_outputs from the DB,
writes it to a temp file, and spawns a background thread running
``run_pipeline()``. Returns the pipeline_id as the job_id immediately.

Before spawning the run thread it pre-flights Docker and git: a not-ready
environment is rejected with HTTP 409 carrying a kind-tagged
``{kind, message, hint}`` payload (the same shape the frontend renders for
pre-run errors), so no orphan run is started.  Multiple pipelines may run
concurrently — each gets its own pipeline_id-scoped workspace.

HTTP 400, with the refusal's text as its detail, answers a document the
preparation refuses: an empty pipeline, an undeclared variable, an
unregistered method, or the validator's refusals. The validator reads
each draft's ``method.yaml`` now, so a draft node that cannot run (no
draft, another folder, its folder gone, an unreadable ``method.yaml``)
and a param or ``param_sets`` value its contract does not accept are
400s too.

A draft node that passes the validator but cannot run is a 409 whose
detail is a ``draft_refused`` payload listing each refusal of
Execution's draft preflight (which reads each draft again, so no Update
is needed): its Registration check fails, its draft run is still
running, it has no selected script, its env cannot be made runnable, or
a link names a slot its contract no longer declares or a required input
it declares is unwired, each naming its node.

get.description:
Return per-node and overall status for a running or completed pipeline.

Queries the ``runs`` table by ``pipeline_id`` and derives overall status.
A job in this server's table reports its run thread's liveness, its
step map, its recorded error and its log. Any other pipeline is reached
through its record (one another process runs, a CLI pipeline among
them, or one this server ran before a restart): its step map comes from
its frozen document, its log from its run directory, and the record's
presence stands for the thread's liveness. Once reached, it is answered
from its rows after its record is gone too.

Args:
    job_id: The pipeline_id returned by the run endpoint.

Returns:
    JSON with ``job_id``, ``overall_status``, ``node_states``, ``thread_alive``,
    ``log``, and ``error`` fields. 404 for an id with neither a job nor
    a record that this server has not reached, and for one that is not
    a pipeline id.

post.description:
Validate a pipeline graph against registered methods in the DB.

The thin wrapper over Execution's ``document_verdict``, the verdict
``wfc check-pipeline`` gives the same document: Graph's structural
check over the substituted document, the validator's refusals and
``draftRefusals``, each draft node that cannot run (no draft or its
folder gone, a failing Registration check, a draft run in progress).

get.description:
Return the pre-substitution pipeline JSON (with variables + {$var}).

Falls back to ``pipeline.json`` (post-substitution) for a run that has
no editable sidecar.
